newsitem.title: USA: Amoco boosts payout, sets buyback and targets. [CORRECTED 21:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Amoco boosts payout, sets buyback and targets. [CORRECTED 21:47 GMT]

text.p: Amoco Corp said it raised its annual dividend to $2.80 per share for 1997 from $2.60 per share for 1996. (Corrects prior dividend rate.)
The increase equalled raising the quarterly payout to $0.70 per share for the first quarter from the preceding quarter's rate of $0.65 per share, the company said.
The oil giant said it plans to repurchase up to $2 billion in common stock over the next two years.
Focused capital and exploration spending for 1997 is expected to be about $4.1 billion, compared to $4.5 billion in 1996, Amoco said.

The company said it set a goal of 10 percent annual earnings growth and will move toward a long-term financial target of 15 percent return on capital employed (ROCE) within five years. "We will enjoy record earnings in 1996," said Amoco chairman Laurance Fuller.

"Some of our major competitors have also made progress. We have improved our financial performance the past three years to achieve our target ROCE range of 11-13 percent ROCE. Now we're setting our sights on 15 percent," Fuller said.
"The higher goal will require continued extraordinary effort by our organization, but I believe we can achieve it within five years," Fuller said.
"We have achieved many of the benefits of our early-1990s restructurings and will continue to reap those benefits with new financial systems and process improvements," he said.

"In 1996 we will replace more than our oil and natural gas production for the fourth consecutive year," he said. "Our goal is to increase our worldwide production of oil and natural gas by at least 25 percent within five years."
Anticipated capital and exploration spending of $4.1 billion for 1997 is below the estimated $4.5 billion the company will spend this year, the company said.

About $2.7 billion, or 65 percent, of 1997 spending is planned for worldwide exploration and production activity, more than half of which will be spent outside North America, the company said. "Key upstream growth areas include Trinidad, Venezuela, Colombia, Azerbaijan, Egypt, the North Sea and the deepwater Gulf of Mexico," it said.
Planned chemical spending of $750 million will go toward completing capacity expansions announced the past two years.
Fuller said the corporation plans to maintain a strong financial capability, with an expected debt to debt plus-equity ratio of 25 to 30 percent.
